title: MP1 · Python OOP Command-Line App
subject: programming-fundamentals
description:
Build an object-oriented command-line app in pairs. Choose ONE: Library Manager, Expense Tracker or Hostel Mess Planner.

COMMON MUST
1. At least 4 classes, including one abstract base class (abc) with two subclasses that override a method, and one @property.
2. JSON persistence: data saved on every change and loaded at start; a missing or corrupted file must not crash the app (start fresh with a warning).
3. Menu-driven CLI with input validation and at least one custom exception.
4. Code split into modules (models.py, storage.py, cli.py, main.py).
5. GitHub Issues for every feature (8+), tracked on a Projects board; both partners commit; work through branches and PRs.
6. README per the documentation checklist (setup, usage, features, class design) with screenshots of the terminal.

LIBRARY: books and members, issue/return with due dates, overdue fine calculation, search by title or author.
EXPENSE: income and expenses by category, monthly summary, budget per category with over-budget warning, CSV export.
MESS PLANNER: weekly menu, student meal opt-in/opt-out, headcount per meal, cost per student per month.

STRETCH: unit tests with unittest or pytest.

Demo in S4: 5 minutes. Both partners must explain any line. Pin the repository on your GitHub profile.

SUBMIT: repo URL; in Notes your app choice and the features you own.

rubric.title: Functionality
rubric.description: All common requirements and the chosen option's features work: data persists across runs, a missing or corrupted JSON file does not crash the app, invalid menu input is rejected, and the custom exception is raised and handled.

rubric.title: Design and code quality
rubric.description: At least 4 sensible classes with an abstract base class, two overriding subclasses and a @property; models free of input/print; code split into models, storage, cli and main; clear names and docstrings.

rubric.title: Git practice (commits, branches, PRs)
rubric.description: 8+ GitHub Issues on a Projects board; features built on branches and merged through PRs that reference their issues; meaningful commits from both partners.

rubric.title: Documentation
rubric.description: README covers purpose, setup and run steps, feature list, class design and who built what, with terminal screenshots; a stranger can run the app from the README alone.

rubric.title: Demo and viva
rubric.description: Five-minute demo of the main flows and error handling, both partners presenting; each partner can explain any line of the code, including the class design and persistence.
